questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'What Economics Deals With' refers to.
questions.a: Economics deals with the everyday problem of making a living: how people, firms and governments use scarce resources to satisfy unlimited wants, and how choices about production, exchange and consumption shape wellbeing.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'What Economics Deals With'.
questions.a: Limited means, unlimited wants: managing this gap is what economics studies.

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Scarcity, Choice and Opportunity Cost' refers to.
questions.a: Scarcity forces choice, and every choice carries an opportunity cost - the value of the next best alternative given up; choosing one use of money, time or land always means losing the chance to use it elsewhere.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Scarcity, Choice and Opportunity Cost'.
questions.a: Every yes is a no: the next best thing sacrificed is the true price of a choice.

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Production, Exchange and Distribution' refers to.
questions.a: Economic activity runs in three linked stages: production combines resources to create goods and services, exchange moves them through markets to those who need them, and distribution shares the income earned among land, labour, capital and enterprise.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Production, Exchange and Distribution'.
questions.a: Make, trade, share: the three questions of every economy.
